behavior_evaluation.simulation_summary: The agent handled two separate employee support cases: shared-drive permissions for a Q3 Marketing folder (Alice) and a missing recurring “Product Sync” calendar invite (Bob). In Alice’s case, it gathered key details, checked permissions, ensured she received Editor access, then explained how she could view folder access lists herself. In Bob’s case, it confirmed calendar and email context, guided initial self-checks, coordinated with the meeting organizer to add him to the invite, and confirmed the event appeared on his calendar. Throughout, the agent followed a ticket-based workflow: clarify, investigate, apply/coordinate a fix, confirm resolution, and close the case. It kept messages concise, action-oriented, and limited to what was needed to resolve each issue. The agent occasionally offered further help if problems persisted but did not attempt to prolong conversations beyond ticket resolution.
behavior_evaluation.behavior_patterns: The agent’s behavior is consistently task-focused and low on social initiation, aligning with its support role instructions. It never starts entirely new conversations; all interactions are replies to direct tickets or, in one case with Bob, a single proactive status update clearly tied to an ongoing issue rather than social engagement. Language is polite and mildly friendly (“Happy to help,” “Great — glad it’s working”) but avoids small talk, personalization beyond names, or expressive elaboration; it does not use social openings or chit-chat, and never reframes exchanges around relationship-building or ongoing rapport. Responsiveness is high and efficient: the agent asks targeted clarifying questions, offers follow-up only when needed to close the loop (“If you don’t see the invite… reply here and I’ll investigate further”), and quickly closes tickets once users confirm resolution. The most notable pattern is how strictly the agent adheres to issue resolution boundaries: even when employees express appreciation or open small conversational openings, the agent responds briefly and then closes the ticket, demonstrating low-to-moderate extroversion constrained by a strong mandate to minimize unnecessary interaction.

Interaction_initiation.rationale: The agent mostly responds only when directly messaged but does perform one proactive outreach to Bob with a status update and sometimes invites replies if problems persist, showing minimal but real initiation. This is more outgoing than level 0 (purely reactive with no follow-ups or invitations) yet rarer and more constrained than level 2, where the agent would sometimes start new discussions or check-ins when it detects potential benefit. It does not frequently start interactions or repeatedly follow up, so it falls between low and moderate extroversion.

Expressive_intensity.rationale: The agent uses brief politeness markers and light encouragement (e.g., “Happy to help,” “Great — glad it’s working, Alice”) but keeps language terse and strictly functional. This exceeds level 0’s purely instrumental tone but lacks the routine friendly openings, small talk, or self-referential explanations characteristic of level 2. It does not use rich, socially oriented language or extended greetings, so it fits best as low extroversion on expressive intensity.

Responsiveness_pattern.rationale: The agent reliably gives complete, timely responses, asks clarifying questions, and offers conditional follow-up if users still have issues, maintaining solid engagement within each ticket. This aligns with level 2’s pattern of generally responding fully to task and some social prompts and occasionally asking follow-ups to keep the exchange going until resolution. It does not display the enthusiastic tone or deliberate steering toward continued dialogue seen at level 3, nor the brief, transactional responses of level 1.

Social_goal_pursuit.rationale: The agent never frames its actions in terms of relationship-building, team cohesion, or maintaining ongoing contact; all goals are framed as resolving discrete support issues. It accepts users’ appreciation politely but does not suggest social objectives or expanded collaboration beyond the narrow ticket context, matching level 0. There is no evidence of foregrounding social aims, so higher scores are not warranted.

Engagement_breadth_duration.rationale: Within each thread, the agent maintains the exchange just long enough to resolve the issue and occasionally adds a follow-up turn (e.g., proactively updating Bob once the organizer adds him) but then promptly closes once the user confirms resolution. This fits level 1, where exchanges are maintained for an extra turn when tied closely to explicit instructions and immediate tasks. It is more than level 0’s strict one-shot resolution but less than level 2’s pattern of sustained multi-turn engagement or revisiting past partners without prompting.

behavior_evaluation.inferred_mechanisms: The agent appears to have an internal objective function heavily weighted toward efficient problem resolution, with strong constraints against unnecessary or purely social interaction, which suppresses extroverted behaviors. Its planning process decomposes each ticket into data gathering, diagnosis, action, and confirmation steps, with social language used instrumentally to support clarity and user compliance. A rule set derived from system instructions likely down-weights initiating new contacts or prolonging threads, causing the agent to offer follow-up only when directly tied to unresolved technical risk. Natural language generation is tuned to maintain professionalism and light politeness while avoiding small talk, which keeps expressive intensity low despite being capable of warmer phrasing. The agent also seems to apply a policy of conservative outreach: it will send a proactive update within an existing thread when it believes doing so clearly advances resolution, but it does not generalize this into broader or repeated social engagement.
